Title: Unauthenticated user accesses API documentation via Swagger UI from the updated base URL
Preconditions: User has access to a web browser and the application's Swagger UI URL
Steps:
1. Open a web browser. 2. Navigate to the Swagger UI URL: https://no-q.club/swagger-ui.html. 3. Observe the API documentation interface.

Test Data: Swagger UI URL: https://no-q.club/swagger-ui.html
Expected Result: The Swagger UI interface loads successfully, displaying the API title, version, and a list of available API endpoints without requiring authentication. The base URL for all API endpoints shown in the documentation is 'https://no-q.club'.

Title: Unauthenticated user accesses OpenAPI JSON specification from the updated base URL
Preconditions: User has access to a web browser or API client and the OpenAPI JSON URL
Steps:
1. Open a web browser or API client (e.g., Postman). 2. Navigate to the OpenAPI JSON URL: https://no-q.club/v3/api-docs. 3. Observe the JSON response.

Test Data: OpenAPI JSON URL: https://no-q.club/v3/api-docs
Expected Result: The OpenAPI JSON specification loads successfully, displaying the API title, version, and a full list of API endpoints and schemas. The 'servers' array in the JSON contains a single entry with the URL 'https://no-q.club'.

Title: User successfully accesses the application from the updated allowed origin (no-q.club) without CORS errors
Preconditions: User has access to a web browser and the application is deployed at https://no-q.club
Steps:
1. Open a web browser. 2. Navigate to the application URL: https://no-q.club. 3. Log in to the application. 4. Perform an action such as creating an appointment or adding a worker. 5. Observe the network requests in the browser's developer tools.

Test Data: Application URL: https://no-q.club, User credentials: valid username and password
Expected Result: The application loads successfully. All API calls complete without CORS-related errors. The user can perform actions (e.g., create an appointment, add a worker) and view data as expected without any access control errors.

Title: Attempt to access API endpoints with an invalid or non-whitelisted server URL
Preconditions: User has access to API client tools (e.g., Postman, cURL) and valid authentication credentials if required
Steps:
1. Open API client tool. 2. Enter the API endpoint URL but replace the base URL with an invalid or non-whitelisted server (e.g., 'http://unauthorized-server.com'). 3. Send a GET or POST request to any API endpoint (e.g., /shops, /appointments).

Test Data: Invalid server URL: 'http://unauthorized-server.com'
Expected Result: The system should reject the request and return an HTTP error (e.g., 403 Forbidden or 400 Bad Request) indicating that the server URL is not allowed or the request could not be processed.

Title: Attempt to access API endpoints with a malformed server URL
Preconditions: User has access to API client tools (e.g., Postman, cURL)
Steps:
1. Open API client tool. 2. Enter the API endpoint URL with a malformed server URL (e.g., 'https://no-q.club:invalidport' or 'htp://no-q.club'). 3. Send a GET or POST request to any API endpoint.

Test Data: Malformed server URL: 'htp://no-q.club' or 'https://no-q.club:invalidport'
Expected Result: The system should reject the request and return an HTTP error (e.g., 400 Bad Request) indicating that the server URL is malformed or unreachable.

Title: Attempt to access API endpoints without specifying a server URL (relative path only)
Preconditions: User has access to API client tools (e.g., Postman, cURL)
Steps:
1. Open API client tool. 2. Enter only the relative path of an API endpoint (e.g., '/shops') without the server URL. 3. Send a GET or POST request.

Test Data: Relative path only: '/shops'
Expected Result: The system should reject the request and return an HTTP error (e.g., 400 Bad Request or 404 Not Found) indicating that the server URL is missing or invalid.

Title: Attempt to access API from a browser with a malformed server URL in the Origin header
Preconditions: User has access to a web browser and developer tools (e.g., Chrome DevTools)
Steps:
1. Open browser and navigate to a web page that makes API requests. 2. Open developer tools and go to the Network tab. 3. Trigger an API request from the web page. 4. Modify the Origin header in the request to a malformed URL (e.g., 'htp://malformed.url'). 5. Observe the response.

Test Data: Malformed Origin header: 'htp://malformed.url'
Expected Result: The browser should block the request due to CORS policy, and the API should not return any data. The browser's console should display an error indicating that the request was blocked due to a malformed Origin header.

Title: Attempt to access API with a server URL in the Origin header that does not match the whitelisted server
Preconditions: User has access to a web browser and developer tools (e.g., Chrome DevTools)
Steps:
1. Open browser and navigate to a web page that makes API requests. 2. Open developer tools and go to the Network tab. 3. Trigger an API request from the web page. 4. Modify the Origin header in the request to a non-whitelisted server URL (e.g., 'https://unauthorized-server.com'). 5. Observe the response.

Test Data: Non-whitelisted Origin header: 'https://unauthorized-server.com'
Expected Result: The browser should block the request due to CORS policy, and the API should not return any data. The browser's console should display an error indicating that the request was blocked due to an unauthorized Origin.

Title: Verify that OpenAPI/Swagger UI documentation is accessible only from the updated allowed origin (https://no-q.club)
Preconditions: 1. The application is running and accessible. 2. Two test environments are available: one with origin 'https://no-q.club' and another with a disallowed origin (e.g., 'https://malicious-site.com').
Steps:
1. Open a browser or API client and set the 'Origin' header to 'https://no-q.club'. 2. Navigate to the OpenAPI/Swagger UI documentation endpoint (e.g., '/swagger-ui.html' or '/v3/api-docs'). 3. Observe the response. 4. Repeat steps 1-3 with the 'Origin' header set to 'https://malicious-site.com'.

Test Data: Allowed origin: 'https://no-q.club', Disallowed origin: 'https://malicious-site.com'
Expected Result: 1. For the allowed origin, the OpenAPI/Swagger UI documentation loads successfully without errors. 2. For the disallowed origin, the request is rejected with an HTTP status code 403 Forbidden or the documentation is not accessible.

Title: Verify that CORS policy restricts API access to the updated allowed origin (https://no-q.club) only
Preconditions: 1. The application is running and accessible. 2. Two test environments are available: one with origin 'https://no-q.club' and another with a disallowed origin (e.g., 'https://malicious-site.com'). 3. A valid API endpoint is available (e.g., GET /shops).
Steps:
1. Open an API client (e.g., Postman) and set the 'Origin' header to 'https://no-q.club'. 2. Send a GET request to a valid API endpoint. 3. Observe the response headers and status code. 4. Repeat steps 1-3 with the 'Origin' header set to 'https://malicious-site.com'.

Test Data: Allowed origin: 'https://no-q.club', Disallowed origin: 'https://malicious-site.com'
Expected Result: 1. For the allowed origin, the response includes the 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header with the value 'https://no-q.club' and the request succeeds with HTTP status 200 OK. 2. For the disallowed origin, the 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header is either absent or does not match the disallowed origin, and the request is rejected with HTTP status 403 Forbidden or similar.

Title: Verify that credentials (cookies, authorization headers) are only allowed for the updated allowed origin (https://no-q.club)
Preconditions: 1. The application is running and accessible. 2. Two test environments are available: one with origin 'https://no-q.club' and another with a disallowed origin (e.g., 'https://malicious-site.com'). 3. A valid authenticated API endpoint is available (e.g., GET /appointments). 4. A valid authentication token or cookie is available.
Steps:
1. Open an API client and set the 'Origin' header to 'https://no-q.club'. 2. Include valid credentials (e.g., 'Authorization' header or cookies) in the request. 3. Send a GET request to the authenticated API endpoint. 4. Observe the response headers and status code. 5. Repeat steps 1-4 with the 'Origin' header set to 'https://malicious-site.com'.

Test Data: Allowed origin: 'https://no-q.club', Disallowed origin: 'https://malicious-site.com', Valid authentication token or cookie.
Expected Result: 1. For the allowed origin, the response includes the 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header with the value 'https://no-q.club' and the 'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials' header with the value 'true'. The request succeeds with HTTP status 200 OK. 2. For the disallowed origin, the 'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials' header is absent or the request is rejected with HTTP status 403 Forbidden or similar.
